# BASH Lab — Bridging AI and Sensing for Health

> Research lab of Prof. Bashima Islam at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (UMass Amherst), building ubiquitous AI systems that learn from motion, audio, physiological and ambient sensor data to support human behavioral well-being. Focus areas: multimodal representation learning, sensor-grounded language models, and resource-constrained (edge / TinyML) inference.

Site: https://bashlab.github.io

## News
- September 2026 — BASH Lab moves to UMass Amherst: The BASH Lab has relocated from Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI) to the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where we continue our research on AI and sensing for health. (https://bashlab.github.io)
- September 2026 — Prof. Bashima Islam receives NSF CAREER Award: The lab received an NSF Faculty Early Career Development (CAREER) Award supporting five years of research (2026-2031), with Bashima Islam as Lead PI. (sponsors.html)
- January 2026 — OWL got accepted in ICLR 2026: OWL shows how an audio language model can infer where a sound is in 3D space (direction and distance) and provide spatially grounded reasoning steps behind its predictions. (https://bashlab.github.io/owl_project/)
- September 2025 — Our paper got accepted in ICASSP 2026: This work was carried out during my internship at Meta Reality Labs, in collaboration with the Audio Research Team, where we studied the characteristics of hair-induced noise in smart glasses audio and developed mitigation strategies for robust real-world wearable audio capture. (https://users.wpi.edu/~sbiswas/assets/publications/26-icassp/ICASSP_26_HNM.pdf)
- September 2025 — Subrata receives Peter B. Meyers Fellowship: This fellowship highlights Subrata’s hard work and excellence in graduate scholarship. (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wpi-electrical-and-computer-engineering-4385b2225_wpi-phd-excellence-activity-7379196307317465088-Tih-?utm_source=social_share_send&utm_medium=member_desktop_web&rcm=ACoAAAgjZbABO4TS_kXaa2F6FK-u5Ex7vOyAWVg)
- September 2025 — EfficientMic got accepted in BuildSys'25: EfficientMic detects aliasing in real time to adapt sampling with just one mic. (Led by Jack) (https://jta2021.wixsite.com/efficientmic)
- September 2025 — NIH NIMH SBIR Phase 2 Awarded:  (https://reporter.nih.gov/search/dA1rsefomUqAkWnzcMSysg/project-details/11393482)
- September 2025 — Mindfulness Meditation and Respiration got accepted in IMWUT/UbiComp'25: This work introduces smartphone-based respiration tracking and mindfulness skill estimation to enhance engagement and usability in digital meditation apps. (Led by Nur) (https://bashlab.github.io/meditite_project/)
- September 2025 — LYNX got accepted in MIT URTC'25 as a Poster: Three high school students developed an open-source multimodal earable for data collection. (Led by Hikmet, Musa, Pranav)
- August 2025 — RAVEN got accepted in EMNLP'25: RAVEN improves multimodal question answering by dynamically gating cross-modal signals—using a single architecture to suppress distractors and resolve modality mismatches. (Led by Subrata) (https://bashlab.github.io/raven_project/)
- July 2025 — LLaSA got accepted in in GENAI4HS Workshop, UbiComp'25: LLaSA combines IMU data with language models to generate interpretable, context-rich answers about human activity using large-scale sensor-caption and QA datasets.. (Led by Shoubornno) (https://bashlab.github.io/llasa_project/)
- June 2025 — LOCUS got accepted in EWSN'25: LOCUS enables robust sound source localization in batteryless systems by intelligently recovering missing multichannel data using deep learning. (Led by Subrata) (https://bashlab.github.io/locus_project/)
- May 2025 — QuaDS got accepted in Interspeech'25: QUADS unifies quantization and distillation to create ultra-efficient spoken language understanding models. (Led by Subrata) (https://bashlab.github.io/quad_project/)
- May 2025 — FATE got accepted in MWSCAS'25: Fate is a novel Fourier-Accelerated CMOS-based Tensor Engine that optimizes matrix multiplication using the Fourier Dot Product. (Led by Jack) (https://bashlab.github.io/fate_project/)

## Research Areas
### Sensing the Future: Bridging Sensors and Language Intelligence
We explore the synergy between sensor data and large language models to create intelligent systems that understand and interpret the world through a fusion of modalities. This research area focuses on developing novel approaches that combine traditional sensing technologies with modern AI to create more intuitive and responsive systems.
Papers: RAVEN (EMNLP'25), LLaSA (GenAI4HS,UbiComp'25)
More: https://bashima.notion.site/sensing-the-future?pvs=4

### Tiny Power, Big Impact: ML for Low-Power Edge Innovation
We pioneer the development of efficient machine learning algorithms for ultra-low-power edge devices, enabling intelligent sensing in resource-constrained environments. This research is crucial for IoT applications and sustainable computing.
Funding: National Science Foundation
Papers: QUADS (Interspeech'25), LOCUS (EWSN'25), FATE (MWSCAS'25), EfficientMic (BuildSys'25), FREEML (EWSN'24)
More: https://bashima.notion.site/tinypower?pvs=4

### Mind Meets Machine: AI Transforming Behavioral Health
We leverage artificial intelligence to revolutionize behavioral health, providing innovative tools for diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment to improve developmental and mental well-being. Our interdisciplinary approach combines AI with healthcare expertise.
Funding: National Institute of Health
Papers: Mindfulness Meditation (IMWUT/Ubicomp'25), Infant SoundTagging (CHASE'24), InfantMotion2Vec (BSN'24), Littlebeats Validation (Sensors'24)
More: https://bashima.notion.site/mind-meets-machine?pvs=4

## Datasets
- AVS-QA: A comprehensive multimodal dataset combining audio, video, and sensor data with question-answer pairs for cross-modal understanding research. (https://huggingface.co/datasets/BASH-Lab/AVS-QA)
- SensorCap: LLM-assisted softly-labelled IMU sensor data captioning dataset with feature summarizations and narrations of human activities. (https://huggingface.co/datasets/BASH-Lab/SensorCaps)
- OpenSQA: Open-source sensor-aware question-answering or instruction-tuning dataset covering IMU data interpretations for human activities. (https://huggingface.co/datasets/BASH-Lab/OpenSQA)
- LargeSet: Sound Source Localization: Large-scale dataset for multichannel sound source localization research with diverse acoustic scenarios and precise ground truth localization information. (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1YbOdBA8p-WI_FRT7ktbiex3TXhZS7igb)
- Aliasing Detection Dataset: A dataset consisting of STFTs derived from the UrbanSound8K Dataset, and ESC50 Dataset which are either aliasing or nonaliasing. (https://github.com/jackadiletta/Aliasing-Audio-STFT-Dataset)

## Models
- RAVEN: Multimodal Reasoning: State-of-the-art multimodal reasoning model combining audio, video, and sensor data for comprehensive scene understanding and cross-modal reasoning. (https://huggingface.co/BASH-Lab/RAVEN-AV-7B)
- LLaSA: Sensor-Language Model: Specialized language model fine-tuned for sensor data interpretation and natural language generation, bridging sensors and human-understandable descriptions. (https://huggingface.co/BASH-Lab/LLaSA-13B)
